# Issue #2602: The compiler reads TOML into a declared struct through a grammar (`Toml::read[T]`)

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2602).

`enhancement`, `selfhosting`, `ready`, `safety` · opened 2026-11-21 · updated 2026-11-22 · 1 comment

Owner, 2026-11-21: a TOML reader built on the grammar mechanism, reading a file into a **declared struct**, not into a dynamic tree: the program states what the file must say, the reader refuses everything else, and only the parser for that type runs ("Ich will ja die Sicherheit haben, dass genau das in der Datei steht, was wir erwarten. Und der Parser dann auch entsprechend schnell arbeiten kann.").

Part of #2505 (its TOML half, built inside the compiler first)
Needs #2599
Found while #2460 (its leftover "A TOML reader for the trust manifest" #2484 needs it)

## Where it stands

* Nikaia has no TOML reader. The compiler reads `nikaia.toml` with the Rust `toml` crate (`Manifest::parse` in `crates/nikaia/src/manifest.rs`, `toml::from_str`) and hands `manifest_parse` (`crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/manifest.nika`) a flat list of `ManifestItem`s, every value as its text.
* The typed-read mechanism exists: a grammar entry with a type parameter, a `match T::kind` in a rule, `members[S](key, value, sep; null:, unknown:)` filling a struct (ADR-grammar-typed-read-v1 D1-D5; tests `grammar_members_builds_a_struct`, `grammar_members_a_member_twice_fails`, `grammar_members_a_missing_field_fails`). A missing field already says `the field `x` is missing at line 1, column 7`.
* A packaged `toml` (#2505) cannot be used across packages yet: `pub grammar` waits for "Build ADR-296 D25: `pub grammar`" (#520). So this grammar lives in the compiler's sources, where its first reader is; moving it into `packages/toml` stays with #2505.
* A map field (`[dependencies]`, `[build.<target>]`, `[library.<name>]`, `[allow.packages.<name>]`) needs the `Map(K, V)` arm, which fails today with NK1250 (#2599).

## Governing decisions

ADR-grammar-typed-read-v1 D1 (an entry takes a type), D2 (`match T::kind`), D3 (`members[S]`), D5 (missing and twice-written members are errors), D6 (`Map(K, V)` with text keys; a format offers the same mechanism, TOML named). Part III 13.3 (what `nikaia.toml` holds). The TOML format itself: TOML 1.0, of which this issue builds the subset below.

## The form

```nika
grammar Toml {
	entry rule read[T: Struct] -> T = ...
}
struct Package { name: String, version: String = "0.0.0", }
struct Doc { package: Package, }
let d: Doc = Toml::read[Doc](text) catch { ... }
```

## To build

1. **`crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/toml.nika`: `grammar Toml` with `entry rule read[T: Struct]`**, lowered by `lower-std` like the other compiler modules. It reads: blank lines and `#` comments (whole line and after a value); `[name]` table headers; `key = value` lines with bare keys (`A-Za-z0-9_-`) and `"quoted"` keys; values by kind: `Text` a basic string `"..."` with the escapes `\" \\ \n \t \uXXXX`, `I64` a decimal integer with an optional sign and `_` between digits, `Bool` `true` / `false`, `List(A)` an array `[a, b,]` across lines with comments between, `Maybe(A)` the value or the key left out, `Struct(_)` an inline table `{ k = v, ... }` or a `[header]` table. The document is the root struct's members: each key line before the first header, each header a member whose value is the table's lines. A table or key written twice is the D5 error. Test `toml_reads_a_declared_struct.nika` (a two-table document with every scalar kind, an array over three lines, an inline table, comments, a quoted key; prints each field) and `toml_refuses_what_the_struct_does_not_say.nika` (`.stdout`: an unknown key, a missing field, a key twice, a string where an integer belongs, each one line with line and column).
2. **Map fields**: a field `collections::BTreeMap[String, V]` (and `HashMap`) is filled from a table's keys, each value read as `V`: `[dependencies]` with `name = { path = "..." }` entries, and a table of tables. Needs #2599 built. Test `toml_reads_a_table_into_a_map.nika` (a map of inline tables and a map of strings, printed in key order).
3. **Dotted headers nest**: `[build.wasm]` after `[build]` is the member `wasm` of the `build` value (a struct field or a map key), `[allow.packages.json]` two levels down. A dotted header whose parent table is not the open one (`[a.b]` before `[a]`, or after `[c]`) is refused with its line and column: the subset reads tables in nesting order, which every `nikaia.toml` in the repository keeps (`git ls-files '*nikaia.toml'`, 44 files). # Issue #2603: Manifest reading uses the Nikaia TOML reader, not the Rust `toml` crate

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2603).

`enhancement`, `selfhosting`, `ready` · opened 2026-11-21 · updated 2026-11-22 · 0 comments

Owner, 2026-11-21: the manifest is read into a declared struct by Nikaia's own TOML reader, so `nikaia.toml` holds exactly what the compiler expects and nothing it silently ignores; the Rust `toml` crate leaves manifest reading.

Part of #2505
Needs #2602
Found while #2460 (unblocks "A TOML reader for the trust manifest" #2484)

## Where it stands

* `Manifest::parse` (`crates/nikaia/src/manifest.rs`) reads the text with `toml::from_str` into a dynamic `toml::Value`, flattens it with `items_of` into `ManifestItem`s (every value as its text), and `manifest_parse` (`crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/manifest.nika`) sorts them into a `ManifestFile`. `value_of` (same Rust file) turns a dependency's text back into a `toml::Value` with `toml::from_str(&format!("v = {text}"))` for `Dependency::Rust` / `Dependency::Nikaia`.
* So the manifest is parsed twice, once dynamically in Rust and once by item in Nikaia, and a key `manifest_parse` does not look at depends on how each section's arm treats it.
* The 44 tracked manifests (`git ls-files '*nikaia.toml'`) use the headers `[package]` (44), `[build]` (19), `[dependencies]` (12), `[rust-library]` (7), `[features]` (3), `[allow]` (2), `[directories]` (2), `[library.sqlite3]` (1); dependency inline tables use only the keys `path`, `type`, `version`. Part III 13.3 (`30-nikaia-tooling.md`) also allows a dependency written as a bare version, `http_server = "1.2"`.

## Governing decisions

ADR-grammar-typed-read-v1 (D1-D6, D13: a typed read; a payload enum is refused for now). Part III 13.3 (the manifest's sections and the dependency forms). ADR-286 D15, D23, D24 (dependency by path, by version). ADR-002 D1 (a Rust crate is passed to Cargo as written).

## To build

1. **`manifest_read(text: String) -> ManifestFile throws Refused`** in `manifest.nika`: declares the manifest's struct (one field per section above, `Maybe` where a section may be left out, `collections::BTreeMap[String, …]` for `[dependencies]`, `[build.<target>]`, `[library.<name>]`, `[features]`, `[allow.packages.<name>]`) and reads it with `Toml::read[...]`, then builds the `ManifestFile` `manifest_parse` builds today, with the same refusals and notes. An unknown section or key is refused with line and column (today it depends on the arm). Test `manifest_read_reads_every_section.nika` (a manifest with every section, printing the `ManifestFile`'s fields) and `manifest_read_refuses_an_unknown_key.nika`.
2. **A dependency is a text or a table**: `name = "1.2"` (by version) and `name = { type = "rust", version = "…" }` / `{ path = "…" }`. A payload enum is refused by D13, so the grammar says it with a rule written for the dependency value (`"\"" … "\""` gives a `DependencyEntry` with only `version`, `{` … `}` reads the struct `{ type: String?, version: String?, path: String?, … }`); the struct names the Cargo keys a Rust dependency may carry (`version`, `path`, `features`, `default-features`, `optional`, `package`, `git`, `branch`, `rev`) and refuses others. If the grammar cannot give one rule two forms by its first byte, that is a `Found:` (gap of kind 2), not a workaround. Test `manifest_read_a_dependency_by_text_or_table.nika`.
3. **The switch**: `Manifest::parse` calls `manifest_read` instead of `toml::from_str` + `items_of` + `manifest_parse`; `items_of` and `value_of` are removed, and `dependency_of` builds `Dependency` from the typed entry. `Dependency::Rust` / `Dependency::Nikaia` keep `toml::Value` only as the form handed to the Cargo writer (`project.rs`), built from the typed entry's fields; that writer's own move is not this issue. `manifest_parse` and `ManifestItem` go if nothing else calls them (`scripts/where.nika`), else the report names the caller. The `it` and compiler tests stay as they are: every tracked manifest reads (checked by `nikaia build` of three packages with `[dependencies]`, `[features]` and `[allow]`).

## Done when

`Manifest::parse` reads `nikaia.toml` through `Toml::read` into the declared struct, an unknown key in any section is refused with its line and column, `items_of` and `value_of` are gone, and the tests pass; the step that removes them carries `Fixes #N`, and the report has a `Found:` line per gap met.

## Files and limits

* Changed: `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/manifest.nika` (and its lowered `.rs`), `crates/nikaia/src/manifest.rs` (the Rust parse path removed; what is left is wiring a lowered function into `Manifest`, which the move into Nikaia allows: CLAUDE.md, *Written in Nikaia only*, a fix that moves code into Nikaia).
* Rust replaced: `Manifest::parse`'s `toml::from_str`, `items_of`, `value_of` (`manifest.rs`). Its `std` counterpart: none (Part III 17 has no TOML reader; the grammar of the reader issue is it).
* Not changed: the other `toml` users (`describe.rs`, `project.rs` writing `Cargo.toml`, `run_fast.rs`, the `orchestrator` crate); each moves with its own issue. The `toml` crate stays a dependency of `crates/nikaia` until they do.
* Must stay identical: the generated `Cargo.toml` of a project (the dependency entries Cargo is handed).

## Ruled out

* Keeping `toml::from_str` and checking keys afterwards: the dynamic read the owner refused, and a second pass.
* A payload enum `Dependency { Version(String), Table(Entry) }` read by `match T::kind`: refused by ADR-grammar-typed-read-v1 D13 for now.

# Issue #2604: drive_proved reads proved.nika's stderr as its summary, so a warning before `proved: ` drops the measurement

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2604).

`bug`, `ready`, `bugs` · opened 2026-11-21 · updated 2026-11-22 · 0 comments

Part of #2302
Found while running the bug lane's driver: no `PROVED` line has been written since the raw path sink check (NK1308) warns on `scripts/proved.nika`. The cause in proved.nika itself is removed by "The small scripts pass the raw path sink check by proof, their nikaia binary named by a literal path" (#2473); this issue makes the driver robust against any warning in the future.

## Symptom

After each push, `drive_proved` (`scripts/drive.nika`) runs `scripts/proved.nika` with `2>&1` and checks `summed.stdout.starts_with("proved: ")`. Every compiler warning proved.nika prints lands before the summary, so the check fails and the driver writes `PROVED <sha> not measured: scripts/proved.nika failed: ...` although proved.nika succeeded. Any new warning in proved.nika or a module it uses drops the measurement in every lane.

## Probe (I5)

Run on `develop` 7a6bd86f5, shared checkout, binary `./target/fast/nikaia`, with a report file holding `bounds in 0 files`:

```
./target/fast/nikaia run scripts/proved.nika -- REPORT > p.out 2> p.err
```

Actual: exit 0; `p.out` starts with `proved: 0/0 indexes (- %), ...`; `p.err` starts with `warning[NK1308]: \`args[1]\` reaches the path \`fs::read_to_string\` opens under \`fs::Root::Anywhere\` ...`. With `2>&1`, as `drive_proved` runs it, the combined output starts with the warning, so `starts_with("proved: ")` is false.

Expected: the driver reads the summary from stdout only and writes the `PROVED` lines; warnings on stderr do not matter while the run succeeds.

## Governing decision (I6)

The proved measurement after each push (#1823, `drive_proved_lines` / `drive_proved_report`). That a warning on stderr must not change what a successful run reports is plainly meant; no decision is needed.

## Cause (I7)

`traced`: `scripts/drive.nika`, `drive_proved`, the line `process::run("sh", ["-c", f"cd '{tree}' && {cache} '{exe}' run scripts/proved.nika -- '{report}' 2>&1"])` mixes stderr into stdout; the next line tests `summed.stdout.starts_with("proved: ")` and passes `summed.stdout` to `drive_proved_lines`.

## Done when

`drive_proved` runs proved.nika without `2>&1`, takes the summary from stdout only, and on failure names the last non-empty stderr line in `PROVED <sha> not measured: scripts/proved.nika failed: <line>`; a test shows a run whose stderr holds warning lines before a successful summary gives the same `PROVED` lines as one without. The commit that finishes step 2 carries `Fixes #N`.

## To build

1. `drive_proved` (`scripts/drive.nika`): drop `2>&1`; test `summed.ok` and `summed.stdout.starts_with("proved: ")` on stdout alone; the failure line uses `drive_tail(summed.stderr, 1)` (or stdout's tail when stderr is empty). Test: extend `tests/compiler/tests/drive_proved.nika` (+ `.stdout`) with a case where warning lines stand on stderr and the summary on stdout; expected the same `--proved-lines` rows as the existing case. The builder chooses how the test reaches the split output (a helper taking stdout and stderr apart, or a stand-in script in `fs::scratch()`).
2. A failing run (exit not 0) gives `PROVED <sha> not measured: scripts/proved.nika failed: <last stderr line>`. Test: one row in `drive_proved.stdout`. Carries `Fixes #N`.

## Files and limits (I11)

Change: `scripts/drive.nika` (`drive_proved` only), `tests/compiler/tests/drive_proved.nika`, `.stdout`. Not: `scripts/proved.nika` (its NK1308 warnings are #2473), the compiler, the NK1308 check.

## Ruled out (I12)

Searching the combined output for the line starting with `proved: `: it keeps warnings and summary mixed and breaks again when a warning line itself starts with that word; stdout and stderr are already separate in `process::run`'s result.

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2622).

`ready` · opened 2026-11-21 · updated 2026-11-21 · 0 comments

Found while building the TOML reader for the compiler (#2602), map of lists. Area: checker (views).

## Probe (`target/fast/nikaia run c1.nika`)

```nika
use std::collections
fn main() throws {
	let t = "a,b"
	let v = t.split(",").collect()
	let mut m: collections::BTreeMap[String, Vec[String]] = collections::BTreeMap()
	m.insert("k", v.clone())
	println(f"{m.len()}")
}
```

Prints:

```
error[NK1343]: Internal compiler error.
  --> c1.nika:6:2
 6 | 	m.insert("k", v.clone())
   = note: Rustc output: mismatched types.
   = note: Expected struct `List<nikaia_std::block::Text>`
   found struct `List<&str>`
```

The same value given to a struct field is refused correctly:

```nika
struct H { xs: Vec[String], }
fn main() throws {
	let t = "a,b"
	let v = t.split(",").collect()
	let h = H { xs: v.clone() }
	println(f"{h.xs.len()}")
}
```

It gives `error[NK1106]: `H.xs` holds a `Vec[String]` whose items are their own, but you're giving it a `Vec[String]` whose items are views.`

## Expected

The checker refuses the call, as it refuses the struct-field case, because `collections::BTreeMap::insert` keeps its `value` after the call returns, and a `Vec[String]` whose items are views is not one of its own (ADR-282 D12, text tiers). It must not hand rustc a program rustc refuses. Which code it gets (NK1102 for a kept argument, or NK1106 as for the field) is not yet checked against the code; the builder takes the one whose text names a kept argument.

## Cause (suspected)

`check_arguments.nika`, the NK1102 branch around line 805 (`state.a_view_kept(found_here, want, named, keeper)`): it looks at whether the argument as a whole is a view, not at the tier of its items. Settling check: a trace of `a_view_kept` for the probe, which should show it returning null.

1. Make the keeping-argument check see a list whose items are views (the item tier the struct-field check NK1106 already reads), and refuse it, with a note that names the items.
2. Add test `tests/compiler/tests/a_kept_list_of_text_views_is_refused.nika` with its `.stderr` (the whole refusal).

The probe is refused at line 6 by the checker under both settings, and no NK1343 comes from it.

# Issue #2636: Tuple spread in a call: `f(..t)` (ADR-call-spread-v1 D1)

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2636).

`ready` · opened 2026-11-21 · updated 2026-11-21 · 0 comments

Part of #449 (subcommands of `main`, option A decided by the owner, 2026-11-21).

**Decision:** [ADR-call-spread-v1](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-call-spread-v1.md) D1 and D4; Part I 5.1 (commit b609876ab).

## Probe

```nika
fn show(file: String, depth: int) {
    println(f"{file} {depth}")
}

fn main() {
    let t = ("areas.md", 2)
    show(..t)
}
```

Today (`target/fast/nikaia check`, b609876ab):

```
error: Expected `)`, `;` or identifier here, but found `.`.
  --> tuple.nika:7:10
```

## Expected

`areas.md 2`. `..t` before the `;` spreads the tuple `t` into the positional arguments in order; it may stand beside written arguments (`f(x, ..t)`, `f(..t, y)`; the spread after the `;` is the struct-spread issue). The call is checked as if written out: a tuple of the wrong length is NK1101, an element of the wrong type NK1102, both naming the spread. A second `..` before the `;`, or `..v` of a value that is not a tuple, is NK1355 (reserved for this lane, listed in Part III 30 under *Decided, not built yet*). The tuple is evaluated once, then taken apart.

## To build

1. **Grammar** in `crates/nikaia/src/parser/mod.rs`, rule `call_args` / `call_args_tail` (around line 3594): an element may be `".." e:expr`. The AST `Expr::Call` in `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/ast.nika` gets the spread as an argument form (e.g. `Expr::Spread { value, id }` allowed only in `args`), so later passes see where it stood. Test `call_spread_tuple_is_parsed.nika` (+ `.stdout`): the probe prints `areas.md 2` once steps 2-3 are in; until then the parser test is the `nikaia check` run of it.
2. **Check** in `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/check_core_args.nika` (`check_core_args_other` and wherever arity and argument types are matched): expand the spread to the tuple's element types before the positional check, so NK1101/NK1102 come out of the existing code; NK1355 for a second spread or a non-tuple. Tests `call_spread_tuple_wrong_length.nika` + `.stderr` (NK1101), `call_spread_tuple_wrong_type.nika` + `.stderr` (NK1102), `call_spread_two_in_one_zone.nika` + `.stderr` and `call_spread_of_a_non_tuple.nika` + `.stderr` (NK1355).
3. **Lowering** (the emit pass for calls, `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/emit_*.nika`): bind the tuple once (`let __s = t;`) and pass `__s.0, __s.1, …`. Test `call_spread_tuple_evaluated_once.nika` + `.stdout`: the tuple comes from a function that prints when called; it prints once; with written arguments before and after the spread, the order is kept.
4. Tooling page: move NK1355 from *Decided, not built yet* into the built list of Part III 30 (the struct-spread half of NK1355 lands with the next issue; say so in the row).

## Done when

All tests above pass and the existing call tests stay green. The commit of step 4 carries `Fixes #N`. A gap met on the way is a `Found:` line in the report (CLAUDE.md, *Moving Rust into Nikaia*), not a workaround.

**Files:** `crates/nikaia/src/parser/mod.rs` (Rust: the grammar lives only there; the same allowance as b39218396; report the lines for #557 / #125), `ast.nika`, `check_core_args.nika`, the call emitter, `docs/specification/30-nikaia-tooling.md`, tests in `tests/compiler/tests/`.

**Facts:** `nikaia test --filter call_spread` from `tests/compiler` runs the new tests; `nikaia test` takes no file arguments.

**Ruled out:** a spread in a struct literal or a list literal, a `Vec` spread into positional arguments (length unknown at compile time), two spreads in one zone: not decided (ADR-call-spread-v1, *Not decided*); a builder meeting a need for them stops with `Result: blocked`.

## Probe

```nika
struct Global {
    /// Prints each step.
    verbose: bool = false,
}

/// Runs one step.
fn run_step(step: String; global: Global = Global {}) {
    println(f"run {step} {global.verbose}")
}

/// Picks the next focus.
fn focus_next(file: String; global: Global = Global {}, depth: int = 1) {
    println(f"focus {file} {depth} {global.verbose}")
}

    command.run(..command.args; ..command.options, global: global)
}
```

`prog --verbose focus-next areas.md` and `prog focus-next areas.md --verbose` both print `focus areas.md 1 true`: a name `main` declares is `main`'s, and reaches the function through the call's written `global: global`. A function option that flattens to a name of `main` with another type is NK1357. `prog --help` prints the usage `prog [OPTIONS] COMMAND …`, `main`'s options, and each command by its command-line name with its first `///` line; `prog focus-next --help` prints that function's help (as D5) followed by `main`'s options.

3. **Reading**: `main`'s options are read wherever they stand, before or after the command word, and a function's own options only after it (`cli.nika`). Test `cli_command_main_option_before_and_after.nika` + `.stdout`.

# Issue #2646: The walk past n loops in a row costs n walks, not 2^n, with a proof that every result stays the same

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2646).

`ledger`, `blocked`, `ci` · opened 2026-11-21 · updated 2026-11-28 · 11 comments

Blocks "The corpus-wide ledger tests are 4-6x slower in CI since the panics inference goes through loops" (#2474). Found by its third run (`docs/briefs/ci/issue-2474-d3.md.run1.report.md`).

Facts: Ledger and bounds proofs

## What happens today

`bounding_past_loop` (`crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/bounds_walk.nika`) walks the statements after a loop twice: `leaves` from the facts past the loop, and, where the loop's invariant settles, `again` from the facts with the invariant; `again` stands only where it proves more. Each of the two walks meets the later loops and walks past each of them twice again, so a run of n loops costs 2^n walks of what follows.

Measured (counter in the lowered `bounds_walk.rs`, `check --bounds`), N loops in a row, each with its own counter (`let mut iK = lo; for j in lo..<hi { if a[j] < K { iK = iK + 1 } }; out.push(a[iK])`):

* loop K is walked past 12·2^(K−1) times; N=8 takes 273 s (226 s invariant searches), N=10 takes 1670 s (1414 s searches).
* `rs2nika_free_methods` in `benches/lowering/source.nika`: 5151 past-loop walks, 3583 searches over 427 s; walks per loop start go 1, 2, 4 … 512; one loop (byte 817536) has 1024 searches over 372 s.

Two routes tried, neither enough:

* **Run 2, a flat trial** (`docs/briefs/ci/issue-2474-d2.patch`, held): `again` is first walked without asking its loops again, and in full only where the trial beats `end`. 0 differences in 2910 D10 decisions of std, 10 loops in 2 s. **Not proved**: a full `again` could stand while its trial does not, where a later loop's invariant settles only under the first loop's facts.
* **Run 3, an exact memo of settled invariants** (not committed): the entry facts of every past-loop walk differ between the `leaves` and `again` walks of each loop before it, so the memo hits 50 % (N loops), 0 % in `rs2nika_free_methods`, and saves at most a third. The misses still double per loop.

## Decision

Supervisor, 2026-11-21: the owner's rule stands, "exactly, not probably": no cut lands that is only measured identical. The cut lands with a proof - an argument in the report, by the code, that for every program it returns exactly the proofs the double walk returns - and a test that pins the shapes where it matters. This keeps every proof, so it is not the owner's trade; if no exact cut is found, the run stops (`Result: blocked`) and the question whether the walk past loops may change what it proves goes to the owner as a decision paper.

Candidates, in order:

1. **Close run 2's gap.** The trial misses only where a later loop's invariant settles under the first loop's facts and not without them. Detect exactly that (the later loop's search is asked from the facts with the invariant wherever its entry facts differ from the trial's in a name it changes) instead of not asking it; prove the trial with that rule returns what the full `again` returns.
2. **One walk from the stronger facts.** If the walk is monotone in its entry facts (more facts, never fewer proofs), `again` proves at least what `leaves` proves, and `leaves` is needed only to find the `wanted` names. Show monotonicity in the code (or name what breaks it - a budget, `poisoned`, `written` - which is then its own finding), and find `wanted` without the full recursive `leaves`.

## To build

1. Read `bounding_past_loop`, `bounding_loop_invariant`, `bounding_stmts` and run 2's patch; write the argument for the chosen candidate in the report first. If neither can be proved, stop as the Decision says, with the case that breaks it as a probe.
2. Build it in `bounds_walk.nika` (Nikaia; the lowered file is output).
3. Check it as well as prove it: run 2's counter over std (every D10 decision: the same proofs), and the 5 shapes of run 2.
4. Add a test in `tests/compiler/tests/` with a `.stdout`: several loops in a row and nested, including a later loop whose invariant needs the first loop's, whose results are the same as before.
5. Measure with callgrind: `Ledger::infer` on `packages/logic/src/sv_strategy.nika` and on `benches/lowering/source.nika`.

## Done when

* The report holds the argument that the cut returns exactly the double walk's results, and the check of step 3 shows no difference.
* N loops in a row cost walks linear in N (the counter shows it), and `rs2nika_free_methods` no longer dominates `source.nika`.
* The corpus tests pass unchanged.

## Files and limits

* `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/bounds_walk.nika` and its lowered output, `tests/compiler/tests/`.
* Do not raise any time limit, skip, split or `#[ignore]` a test, or weaken a proof. Do not take the performance lane's issues.

Research result: is there an exact linear walk (one where every result stays the same)?

**Not today.** The losing walk leaves state behind that `BoundsMark` does not restore: return summaries, `axioms`, fresh-name counters, `flagged`, `leaving` and the arena. Later questions read that state. An exact speed-up could only share work where two walks reach a loop in the same state, and that never happens, because these fields only grow.

Ideas we checked and ruled out:
- Splitting the decision into one comparison per segment between loops. Not exact: a later loop can flip the decision.
- Stopping `again` early once it can no longer win. Not exact: the cut-short walk leaves different state behind.

The route, in order:
1. Answer each solver question once per function (#2885). This is exact and keeps the 2^n walks, but cuts their cost.
2. Make the losing walk leave nothing behind (#2886). This is what ADR-361 D10 means: a losing walk does not stand. It can only gain proofs.
3. After #2886, measure how often walks reach a later loop in the same state, compared up to fresh names. If the rate is high, merging those walks gives a linear walk that is exact relative to the state after #2886. That becomes a new issue once the measurement is in.

Options B, C and D of the decision paper stay out under the owner's rule.

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2679).

`compiler`, `views`, `ready`, `bugs` · opened 2026-11-22 · updated 2026-11-22 · 0 comments

Found in the run of #2649 (report `docs/briefs/performance/issue-2649.md.report.md`), HEAD c4087853c, `target/fast`.

## Probe

```nika
use std::fs
fn tally(path: String) -> String throws {
    let mut trigger: String = ""
    for line in fs::read_to_string(path, fs::Root::Anywhere).lines() {
        let (_, after) = line.split_once("=") ?? continue
        trigger = after
    }
    return trigger
}
```

**Actual:** NK1343 "Internal compiler error ... cannot return value referencing temporary value".

**Expected:** NK1105, a view assigned to an owning `String`. The same assignment written without the tuple `let` gives NK1105 today:
- `trigger = line.trim()`
- `let pair = line.split_once("=") ?? continue; trigger = pair.1`

## Cause (suspected, not traced)

The tuple `let` in `check_binds.nika` (`tuple_let` / `a_tuple_part_is_lent`) drops the view flag of a part of a view tuple.

## To build

1. Run the probe on today's `develop` first (it may already be fixed).
2. Trace the cause and fix it in `check_binds.nika`.
3. Add a test in `tests/compiler/tests/`: the probe with its `.stderr` naming NK1105.

## Done when

The probe gives NK1105, and the test pins it.

# Issue #2694: An argument of process::run whose start is from outside is a raw sink, proved by process::is_operand or a literal "--" (ADR-raw-sinks-1 D18)

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2694).

`ready`, `safety` · opened 2026-11-22 · updated 2026-11-23 · 8 comments

Owner's decision on #1939 (2026-11-22, alternative C), written as ADR-raw-sinks-1 D18: the start of each element of `process::run`'s `args` is a raw sink. An element whose first part is from outside is refused, `NK1308`, unless `process::is_operand(part)` guards it, a literal `"--"` stands earlier in the list, or the manifest allows `untrusted-option`.

## Probe

On develop 2026-11-22, a file `opt.nika`:

```nika
use std::process
use std::cli

fn main() throws {
    let name = cli::args().nth(1) ?? ""
    process::run("rm", [name])
}
```

**Expected** (ADR-raw-sinks-1 D18 item 1): `nikaia check opt.nika` refuses the call, `NK1308`, at `name`, and the help offers `process::is_operand(name)` or `"--"` before it.

**Actual**: it builds. `prover_walk.nika` treats only the `program` of `process::run` as a sink (D10); `std::process` has no `is_operand`, and the manifest reader knows no `untrusted-option`.

## Cause

Traced: D10 was built by #2217 with the arguments explicitly outside the rule ("each reaches the program as one word"); D18 changes that.

## Status (2026-11-22, updated 14:20)

Built by 4225dbeec (accepted as partial): item 1's `is_operand` and its guard, and items 2, 3, 6 and 7.

**Changed since by D18 item 6** (local commit 653abd8bb, Part of #2722): a literal `"--"` **no longer proves** the elements after it, and `process::is_operand` refuses a leading `/` as well as `-`. Read the `"--"` route in the text below as withdrawn. A file passes as `"./" + name` or as `root.join(name).path().to_text()` (D18 item 4), or behind an `is_operand` guard.

**Left:**
- Item 4: the run-time check under warn. It needs plumbing like D7's raw_paths. #2722's item 4 waits on the same work.
- Item 1's hand-back proof of a checking function. `OutsideProof` in prover_calls.nika is path-specific today.
- Item 5: the NK1308 warnings in our own code. That is the 191 counted here, plus 25 more that 653abd8bb opened in scripts/ by dropping the `"--"` proof: agent.nika 540-655, commit.nika 154-484, cycle.nika 135/157, status.nika 100, drive.nika +13. scripts/ went from 162 to 187 warnings in warn mode.
  - Each site is proved by an `is_operand` guard, a `"./"` prefix or a root-joined path. Never by an allow, and never by `trusted:`.
  - Git reads a leading `./` as a path, so it is the natural form for git pathspecs.
  - #2723 (a shell as the program) rewrites some of the same calls. Make sure the proofs still hold under that rule.

## To build

1. `process::is_operand(text: ref String) -> bool` in `std::process`, written in Nikaia: true when the text does not start with `-` (the empty text holds it). It is a guard predicate like `path::is_below` (D14): after `if process::is_operand(x)` and after `if !process::is_operand(x) { ...; return/exit }`, `x` is proved for this sink, and a function that checked it hands back its proof.
2. The prover (`crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/prover_walk.nika`): for each element of `process::run`'s second argument, written as a list literal, the element's first part is asked. A first part that is not outside passes whatever follows (`"--output=" + name`, `f"-I{dir}"`, a path of a `Dir`, D18 item 4). An outside first part passes when proved by item 1 or when a literal `"--"` element stands earlier in the same list; otherwise `NK1308` under key `untrusted-option`. An `args` that is not a list literal is outside as a whole when any value pushed into it is (as `a_list_filled_from_outside_is_outside` does today) and is then refused unless every pushed outside value was proved, or a literal `"--"` was pushed first.
3. The manifest key `untrusted-option` in `manifest.nika` (`[allow]`, `[allow.packages.NAME]`, `--allow=KEY`, `--allow=NAME:KEY`, `--trust` lists it), the same way `untrusted-program` is read.
4. The run-time check under `raw-sinks = "warn"` (D7): `process::run` throws `io::IoError::Other` naming the argument, before anything starts.
5. Our own code: before switching the rule on, count the calls it refuses in the compiler, `packages/`, `examples/`, `tools/`, `scripts/` and `benches/` (by a build under `raw-sinks = "warn"`) and list the count in the report. Each one is fixed by a proof (`is_operand` guard or `"--"`, or the value made under a `Dir`), never by `trusted:` and never by an `[allow] untrusted-option` line; an `[allow]` line only where taking an option from outside is what the tool is for, named in the report.
6. Tests in `tests/compiler/tests/`, each with its `.stdout` / `.stderr`: `an_outside_argument_of_process_run_is_a_raw_sink` (refused, the help text), `an_argument_proved_an_operand_passes`, `a_literal_double_dash_proves_the_arguments_after_it` (and one before it stays refused), `an_option_the_program_wrote_passes_with_an_outside_value` (`"--output=" + name`), `untrusted_option_in_the_manifest_admits_the_call` (with `raw_sinks_manifest_keys` extended).
7. Website and guide: where `process::run` is described, the rule and its example; drop "specified, not built yet" from Part III 17 (`std::process`) once it passes.

## Done when

The probe is refused with `NK1308` and passes after `if !process::is_operand(name) { process::exit(2) }` and with `["./" + name]` (the `"--"` route was withdrawn by D18 item 6). The tests of item 6 pass, every existing raw-sink test passes with its expected output unchanged, our own code builds under the rule with the count of item 5 fixed by proofs, and the last commit carries `Fixes #N`.

crates/nikaia-std/src/std/process.nika (or where `std::process` lives), crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/prover_walk.nika, crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/manifest.nika and their lowered `.rs`, tests/compiler/tests/, docs/specification/30-nikaia-tooling.md, guide/ and website/ where `process::run` appears.

# Issue #2697: The bounds walk walks a loop's rest again within one pass from an equal state

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2697).

`blocked`, `solver` · opened 2026-11-22 · updated 2026-11-22 · 1 comment

Part of #2474
Found while #2652
After #2711

## Goal

Within one pass of the bounds walk, a walk past a loop whose complete entry state equals that of an earlier walk in the same pass is not walked again: its outcome and its side effects are replayed. The walk proves exactly what it proves today (owner rule).

## Today (read in the code)

* `bounding_past_loop` in `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/bounds_walk.nika` (ADR-361 D10) walks the rest of the body twice past each loop (`leaves` and `again`, the second from the invariant facts `bounding_loop_invariant` found) and keeps `again` only where it stands. The state saved and restored around the walks is `BoundsMark` (`bounding_mark` / `bounding_back`, same file).
* Fields of `BoundsWalk` outside `BoundsMark` that a walk changes: `flagged`, `leaving`, `settled_loops`, `turn_rows`, `assumed_read`, `self_read`, `found_read`. Fresh names come from the counters `entries` and `codes`. Terms live in a `logic::TermArena` that is not hash-consed, so a term id says nothing of the term's structure.

## Measured (commit 15c267871, instrumented scratch build of `bounding_past_loop` logging a hash `kst` of the facts, alpha-renamed, plus every `BoundsMark` field and the written, poisoned and missed-goal sets, and `ko` of the outcome)

| Memo key and scope, `packages/logic/src/sv_strategy.nika` | Duplicate calls | Calls skipped | Inconsistent outcomes |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `kst`, within a pass | 1760 of 7989 | 2537 (32 %) | 0 |
| `kst`, across passes | 6184 | 7117 | 390 |
| facts only, across passes | | | 3033 |
| facts only, within a pass | | | 25 |

In loopsN (below, N loops) the 2^N − 1 entry states within a pass are all distinct (each `again` starts from new invariant facts): 0 saved there. In `sv` 99.2 % of the walks lie at nesting ≥ 3. The invariant searches with the full key (entry facts plus walk state) repeat 1604 of 2106 times in `sv` (82 % of the proofs asked in searches), nearly all across passes, which the kept-proof issue (#2711) removes in part (measure again after it); within a pass this memo covers them.

```nika
fn loops(a: ref Vec[i64], lo: i64, hi: i64) -> Vec[i64] {
	assert(0 <= lo)
	assert(lo <= hi)
	assert(hi <= a.len())
	let mut out: Vec[i64] = []
	let mut i1 = lo
	for j in lo..<hi { if a[j] < 1 { i1 = i1 + 1 } }
	out.push(a[i1])
	let mut i2 = lo
	for j in lo..<hi { if a[j] < 2 { i2 = i2 + 1 } }
	out.push(a[i2])
	let mut i3 = lo
	for j in lo..<hi { if a[j] < 3 { i3 = i3 + 1 } }
	out.push(a[i3])
	return out
}

fn main() {}
```

`nikaia check --bounds loops3.nika` (target/fast, built 2026-11-22, shared checkout; checked with `scripts/probe.nika --check --file`, exit 0): `6 indexes, 3 proved; 3 operations, 3 proved`; the three `a[iK]` stay `checked: a counter the loop on line 7 changes, with no bound tied to its turns or to another counter (ADR-361 D13, #1634)`, 1.2 s. `loopsN` below is this program with N loops.

## Why it is exact

The walk is deterministic: a walk with equal complete input gives equal output. Complete input needs all four: (1) the state outside `BoundsMark` listed above in the key, or replayed from the entry; (2) the key alpha-renamed over the `entries` / `codes` names and the stored outcome renamed back to the current counters; (3) a structural key of the terms, not their ids; (4) the round inputs (`context.returns`, the summaries of other functions, `assumed`, `assumed_ends`, `collecting`), which the memo held only within one pass keeps fixed. Without (4) the across-pass figure shows 390 inconsistent outcomes; without the walk state, 25 within a pass.

## Cause

`traced` for the cost (the calls counted above; 81-84 % of the Ir is the invariant search inside these walks, callgrind on `chained` and loops6). Which repeat inside a pass gives the 1760 duplicates (the same loop reached by the `leaves` and `again` walks of an outer loop with equal state) is `suspected`; item 1 shows it.

## To build

1. A structural, alpha-renamed key of a walk's complete entry state (facts, `BoundsMark`, the outside fields above, the position), behind `NIKAIA_BOUNDS_MEMO=count`: a stderr line per pass with the duplicates it would skip. Test: `tests/compiler/tests/the_walk_memo_counts_repeated_walks.nika` with `.stdout`, `.stderr` and `.bounds` (a body of two nested loops each followed by a third loop, so an inner state repeats; the builder writes it and checks with `scripts/probe.nika --check`). If no repeat inside a pass shows on it or on `sv` after the kept-proof issue (#2711) landed, stop: `Result: blocked`, `Found:` the counts.
2. The memo: keep each walk's outcome and its side effects on the outside fields and the counters, renamed to the key's names; on a hit, replay them renamed back instead of walking. Test: the same `.bounds` rows as without the memo on the test of item 1, on loops3 above, and every `*.bounds` test unchanged.

## Done when

`nikaia check --bounds` and `lower-std --bounds` give byte-identical reports before and after, `bytes::the_corpus_needs_no_tether` passes, and the calls of `bounding_past_loop` within a pass on `sv_strategy.nika` fall by the share item 1 measured (32 % at 15c267871); the commit of item 2 carries `Fixes #N`. The report gives a `Found:` line per finding.

## Files and limits

* Changes: `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/bounds_walk.nika` and its lowered `bounds_walk.rs` (output). No new Rust.
* Must not change: any `--bounds` row, `proofs_answers.nika` (the query-key issue's file, #2696).
* Limits: `most_facts()` 48 and 256 held facts: the walk is not monotone, so only an exact state repeat may be replayed. The memo is per pass and per body; its size is bounded by the walks of that pass (2^n − 1 entries at most). Time before: `check --bounds` loops6 27.5 s, `sv_strategy.nika` 47.7 s (target/fast at 15c267871, wall).

Facts: Ledger and bounds proofs, Prover, Measuring

## Ruled out

* A memo on the facts alone: 25 inconsistent outcomes within a pass, 3033 across (NOT EXACT).
* A search cache keyed by the loop's names only: 4 keys gave different results (NOT EXACT).
* A memo across passes: measured under 1 % (#2695, closed); the repeated whole walk is #2711.
* Skipping `again` or cutting the rest of the walk to the loop's cone: can lose a proof (NOT EXACT); the cone-factorised decision issue covers the exact form.

# Issue #2698: Decision: may the bounds walk factorise its stand rule by loop cones under a guard, after a written proof? (ADR-361 D10)

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2698).

`decision`, `solver` · opened 2026-11-22 · updated 2026-11-22 · 0 comments

Part of #2474
Found while #2652

## The question

The bounds walk is 2^n in the number of loops in a row (ADR-361 D10: two walks past each loop). Should it get a cone-factorised stand rule that is linear where a run-time guard holds and today's walk where it does not, once a written proof shows the guard keeps every proof? Owner decision: it changes the walk's decision rule, and the owner rules that no proof is traded for speed.

## Today (read in the code)

`bounding_past_loop` in `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/bounds_walk.nika` walks the rest of the body once from the facts that leave the loop (`leaves`) and once from the invariant facts `bounding_loop_invariant` found (`again`), and keeps `again` only where it stands: where it proves at least as many of the open goals of the whole rest of the walk. Each walk does the same at every later loop, so a body of N loops in a row is walked 2^N − 1 times per pass, in 4 checks passes and 8 returns passes: exactly 12·(2^N − 1) calls.

## Measured (commit 15c267871)

| Probe | Calls C / R | `check --bounds` |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| loops1 | 4 / 8 | 0.14 s |
| loops3 | 28 / 56 | 1.13 s |
| loops6 | 252 / 504 | 27.5 s |
| `packages/logic/src/sv_strategy.nika` | 4505 / 3484 | 47.7 s |

Time grows 2.6-3.1 times per loop; the 2^n dominates from n = 3. Of 16 831 functions, 463 have at least 3 loops finished before some statement, 74 at least 6 (largest 16, in `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler`). In `sv`, 99.2 % of the walks lie at nesting ≥ 3.

```nika
fn loops(a: ref Vec[i64], lo: i64, hi: i64) -> Vec[i64] {
	assert(0 <= lo)
	assert(lo <= hi)
	assert(hi <= a.len())
	let mut out: Vec[i64] = []
	let mut i1 = lo
	for j in lo..<hi { if a[j] < 1 { i1 = i1 + 1 } }
	out.push(a[i1])
	let mut i2 = lo
	for j in lo..<hi { if a[j] < 2 { i2 = i2 + 1 } }
	out.push(a[i2])
	let mut i3 = lo
	for j in lo..<hi { if a[j] < 3 { i3 = i3 + 1 } }
	out.push(a[i3])
	return out
}

fn main() {}
```

`nikaia check --bounds loops3.nika` (target/fast, built 2026-11-22, shared checkout; checked with `scripts/probe.nika --check --file`, exit 0): `6 indexes, 3 proved; 3 operations, 3 proved`; the three `a[iK]` stay `checked: a counter the loop on line 7 changes, with no bound tied to its turns or to another counter (ADR-361 D13, #1634)`, 1.2 s. `loopsN` below is this program with N loops.

## The idea

The choice at loop L compares the proof counts of two subtrees. Split the open goals after L into cones: the goals reading names a loop changes, grouped so that cones share no loop. Suppose the guard holds:

* no query reached `most_facts()` (48) or 256 held facts (no ranking dropped a fact);
* `invariant.past` keeps the facts of every name outside L's cone unchanged;
* no flag and no `.len()` fallback was used in the walk.

Then a subtree's count is a sum over cones, and the choice at L depends only on L's cone. Each cone costs 2^(its loops) walks; in loopsN that is n cones of one loop: 2n walks instead of 2^n − 1. Where the guard fails, the walk is today's walk.

## Options

1. **Build it after a written proof.** First the proof (an ADR text under ADR-361) that under the guard the factorised choice equals today's at every loop, and that the guard is checked completely at run time; then the build, with `--bounds` reports byte-identical on the corpus and the guard's fallback counted. Linear where the guard holds; today's cost elsewhere.
2. **Keep today's walk** and take only the exact constant factors (the pass-skip (#2695), query-key (#2696) and walk-memo (#2697) issues of the solver lane): up to 4 times fewer walks, 10-25 % cheaper walks, still 2^n.
3. **A cheaper rule that may prove less** (skip `again`, cut to the cone without the guard, the trial-plus-rerun hybrid as measured): ruled out by the owner rule; listed only so the choice is complete.

## What is not shown yet

* That the guard is complete: that no other coupling (the stand rule over all goals, the fact ranking, the written / poisoned sets, `context.returns`) links two cones.
* How often it holds: `sv` has up to 108 facts at entry (mean 29), so the cap guard would often fail there; loopsN has 54-67 at entry, above 48, so even loopsN may fall back. Measuring the share of loops where the guard holds is the first step of option 1.

## Recommendation

Option 2 now (its issues are `ready`), and option 1 as a research step: a builder measures, behind a counter, how often the guard holds on the corpus and `sv`; only if it holds for most 2^n bodies is the proof written and the build filed. Nothing that may prove less is built.

## Cause

`traced`: the walk counts above (12·(2^N − 1), counted in an instrumented build) and callgrind (the invariant search inside these walks is 81-84 % of the Ir on `chained` and loops6).

## To build (if option 1 is chosen)

1. A counter behind `NIKAIA_BOUNDS_CONES=count`: per loop, whether the guard holds and the cones. Test: `tests/compiler/tests/the_walk_counts_its_cones.nika` with `.stdout`, `.stderr`, `.bounds` (loops3 above).
2. The proof as ADR text under ADR-361 (supervisor; owner approval).
3. The factorised rule under the guard, falling back to today's walk. Test: the `.bounds` rows of item 1 unchanged and every `*.bounds` test unchanged.

## Done when

The owner chose an option; for option 1, `nikaia check --bounds` and `lower-std --bounds` give byte-identical reports before and after item 3, `bytes::the_corpus_needs_no_tether` passes, and loops6 takes at most 2·6 walks per pass where the guard holds; the commit of item 3 carries `Fixes #N`. The report gives a `Found:` line per finding.

## Files and limits

* Changes: `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/bounds_walk.nika` and its lowered file (output); the ADR-361 text. No new Rust.
* Must not change: any `--bounds` row.
* Limits: `most_facts()` 48, 256 held. Time before: loops3 1.2 s (target/fast, shared checkout, `develop` 79ba87701), loops6 27.5 s, `sv_strategy.nika` 47.7 s (15c267871).

Facts: Ledger and bounds proofs, Prover, Measuring

## Ruled out

* Skipping `again`: its entry facts are neither a subset nor a superset of `leaves` in 939 of 1050 cases in `sv` (NOT EXACT).
* A cone cut without the guard: `invariant.past`, the 48-fact ranking and the stand rule couple the cones (NOT EXACT).
* Running checks and returns in one walk: the stand rule counts both kinds of goal together (NOT EXACT).
* The trial-plus-rerun hybrid as it stands: +28 % walks on the corpus, +47 % on `sv`.

# Issue #2703: Pin winnow-grammar to main a310181: fewer allocations per stream, context lent to a step

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2703).

`wip`, `yaml` · opened 2026-11-22 · updated 2026-11-23 · 12 comments

## Why

Nikaia pins winnow-grammar at `e417f40` (`Cargo.toml:33`, `crates/unsafe/task-block/Cargo.toml:18`). Its `main` is at `a310181` (merge of its PR #47), 22 commits later, and is faster (owner, 2026-11-22). From its CHANGELOG:

* A short stream allocates less (55dbdf0, fd437f7); an interner takes one allocation (fe9f5cf).
* A stream lends its 256-byte `ParseContext` to each step instead of moving and cloning it (3c8d402, 6fc4c7e): `stream_profile list` (20 000 short streams) -10.3 % / -17.9 % (default / one codegen unit), `slice_profile list` -9.4 % / -23.2 %.
* `parse_<rule>_str` / `_str_each` (fe2e151) and a slice entry (90be573, 2271a02): a stream over input that is all in memory reads it in place, nothing copied; `str_profile list` 75.3M against 87.1M.

The version stays `0.2.0`.

## Breaking change to adapt to

winnow-grammar d5eb090: in a grammar with a `#[stream]` rule, the rules are generic over the context type `C: winnow_grammar::Ctx`. An `extern rule` that such a grammar calls takes `fn r<'a, C: Ctx>(i: &mut ParseInputOf<'a, C>)` and reaches the state with `i.state.cx()` / `cx_mut()`; a rule named with a turbofish names the context (`parse_x::<ParseContext<()>>()`). Grammars without `#[stream]` are unchanged.

Where this may touch Nikaia: the Rust that `emit_grammar.nika` / `emit_core_leaves.nika` write for a `@stream` grammar (`emit_stream_reader`, `emit_stream_walk`), the parser's `extern rule`s in `crates/nikaia/src/parser/mod.rs` (only if that grammar has a stream rule), and the users of the stream API in `crates/nikaia-std/src/process.rs`, `net.rs`, `crates/unsafe/polled/src/lib.rs`, `crates/nikaia/tests/it/{project,sockets}.rs`.

## To build

1. Measure before, with callgrind (`docs/measuring.md`): the yaml stream benchmark (`deep.yaml`, last 188.7M after the e417f40 pin, CHANGELOG 0.0.1505), the `parse` benchmark, and one short-stream case (many small `@stream` parses).
2. Set `rev = "a310181"` in `Cargo.toml` and `crates/unsafe/task-block/Cargo.toml`; `cargo update -p winnow-grammar -p winnow-grammar-macro` (every winnow-grammar crate in the lock) in the root and in `crates/unsafe/task-block`.
3. Build. Where the context-type change breaks the emitted Rust, change the emitter (`emit_grammar.nika` / `emit_core_leaves.nika`) and re-lower; no hand edit in `lowered/`. Where a `@stream` grammar in Nikaia calls an `extern rule`, give it the context type as above.
4. Where the new `_str` / slice entry fits a parse over text that is already in memory (a `@stream` grammar run over a `String`), use it in the emitted code, if it is a one-line choice in the emitter; otherwise file it as its own issue with the measurement.
5. Measure after, same cases; the report gives both figures per case.
6. Tests: the stream and grammar tests in `tests/compiler/tests/` and the touched crates' tests.

## Done when

* Both manifests and both lock files name `a310181`; build, clippy and the touched tests are green.
* The report gives callgrind before / after for yaml, parse and the short-stream case, and no case is slower by more than 0.5 % without a stated reason.

## Notes

The previous pin bump was the yaml lane's (#2437); it holds #2435 and #2419, which this bump does not finish. No change to the Cargo profiles, so no warning to the CI lane is needed.

# Issue #2708: A `for` over a `@stream` call runs its body as the parser's `each`, and the items view the input (ADR-grammar-typed-read-v1 D7)

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2708).

`blocked`, `yaml` · opened 2026-11-22 · updated 2026-11-22 · 10 comments

Part of #1548
Found while #2426

## What it is

ADR-grammar-typed-read-v1 D7, as rewritten after the owner's decision on #2426 (2026-11-22): an item of a `@stream` entry views the input it is parsed from (ADR-views-v4 D5), and the compiler chooses how each walk runs. This issue builds the first method, the one the yaml benchmark and part 6 of the yaml goal need: a `for` over a `@stream` call runs its body as the parser's `each`, with no thread and no channel.

Today `__nikaia_walk_<book>__<rule>` (`emit_stream_walk` and the batched handoff in `crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/emit_grammar.nika`, lines 379 and 970) takes the input by move, parses on a spawned thread and hands owned items over a channel. So yaml's `Event` cannot hold views: the stream needs its fields owned, and the ledger lists a field tethered or owned per type. That blocks "yaml: events and nodes refer to their scalars in the input instead of copying each into a String" (#2417). On yaml-deep the stream counts 188.7M against 157.6M in memory (callgrind, checks off).

## To build

1. **Push at a direct `for`.** A `for` whose iterable is a `@stream` call, or a local bound to one that this `for` alone walks, once, in the same function, lowers to `parse_<rule>_slice_each` with the input lent and the body as the `each` closure.
   - The input is lent, not moved; a temporary (`Yaml::events(Bytes(...))`) lives for the `for`.
2. **Control flow out of the body.**
   - `continue` returns `ControlFlow::Continue`; `break` returns `ControlFlow::Break`, as today.
   - `return`, `throw`, a labelled `break` or `continue` to an outer loop, and a parse error are carried out of the closure as the break's reason and acted on after the call.
3. **Items view the input.** An item's text fields are views of the input (ADR-views-v4 D5), listed `tethered` in the ledger; an item kept beyond the input is refused as any view is, with `.clone()` named.
4. **The other uses, until the general method is built.** A `@stream` call held and passed on, handed back, stored, given to a task, combined or walked twice keeps today's thread where its item type holds no view. Where it does, the use is refused with `NK1355` (reserved here), naming the use and the build issue of the general method.
5. **Tests** in `packages/yaml/tests/`: the existing `events_stream`, `events_break` and `events_stream_whole_input` pass unchanged. New tests for:
   - an item kept past the loop with `.clone()`;
   - `return` and `throw` from inside the loop;
   - a labelled `break` to an outer loop;
   - `NK1355` on a stream handed back from a function whose item holds a view, with its `.stderr`.
6. **Count** yaml-deep's stream against the in-memory path with callgrind (`docs/measuring.md`) before and after, and give both counts in the commit message.

## Done when

`for e in yaml::Yaml::events(input)` lowers to the parser's `each` with no thread, as the generated Rust shows. The tests of item 5 are green. The commit message gives the stream's count on yaml-deep before and after, beside the in-memory count.

# Issue #2709: The other methods of a `@stream` walk: scoped thread, owned at the boundary, the Rust reader's owned form, walking twice, the ledger's line (ADR-grammar-typed-read-v1 D7)

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2709).

`ready` · opened 2026-11-22 · updated 2026-11-22 · 1 comment

Part of #2426
After #2708

## What it is

ADR-grammar-typed-read-v1 D7, as rewritten after the owner's decision on #2426 (2026-11-22), makes a `@stream` call a sequence like any other. It may be held, passed on, handed back, stored, given to a task and combined. An item views the input, and the compiler chooses how each walk runs. "A `for` over a `@stream` call runs its body as the parser's `each`" (#2708) builds the direct `for` (push) and refuses the other uses where the item holds a view (`NK1355`). This issue builds the methods for those uses, so nothing is refused.

## To build

1. **Scoped thread.** A held or passed sequence with one consumer the compiler cannot see through, and a `for` whose body pauses, run the parser on a thread that borrows the input (`std::thread::scope`), so items keep their views.
2. **Owned at the boundary.** A sequence that outlives the input's loan (stored, given to a task, sent away) runs on its own thread with the input owned. Its items are converted to an owned form of the item type where they leave the thread, generated beside it.
   - `NK1355` and its interim refusals go.
3. **The Rust reader** (`G::<rule>_reader(r)`) hands out the owned form of item 2; `NK1345` applies to that form.
4. **Walked twice.** A held sequence walked twice parses twice, and the ledger names it. The compiler may collect it once where it sees that is cheaper.
5. **The ledger** names, per walk, the method chosen and where a copy is made. A lint names a walk that fell to the copying method.
6. **Tests** in `tests/compiler/tests/` for each row of D7's table, with the ledger's line.

## Done when

Each use D7 names (held, passed on, handed back, stored, given to a task, combined, walked twice) compiles and runs with items that view the input where the loan covers the walk. `NK1355` is retired. The ledger names the method per walk, and a test per row is green.

# Issue #2721: Kani mode in the emitter: the switch, harnesses and a byte-identical guard

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2721).

`blocked`, `safety` · opened 2026-11-22 · updated 2026-11-22 · 0 comments

Records ADR-proof-kani-v1 (Kani checks the prover's proofs on the emitted Rust, in a mode of its own); the second of its six issues.
Needs #2720

## Goal
A switch that makes the emitter write a crate Kani can check — the crate attributes and one harness per checked function — while every build without the switch writes byte-identical Rust. No contracts yet: they come in the two issues after this one.

## Governing decision
ADR-proof-kani-v1 D1 (a mode of its own; byte-identical output without it; nobody pays for it who does not run it), D6 (harnesses under `cfg(kani)`, the crate attributes under `cfg_attr(kani, …)`). ADR-001 D1 (output is Rust).

## Today (read in the code)
* The tests' lowering is asked for with `--bounds` in `project_tests.nika` (`host.explained(["--bounds"], entry, own, main)`); there is no Kani switch anywhere.
* A function's head is written by `emit_fn_signature` (`emit_function.nika`); the crate's head by the lowering's crate writer, which the builder finds (`scripts/where.nika`).

## To build
1. **The switch.** A setting `kani` that the emitter reads once into its state (where `--bounds` is read; the builder names the field). Off by default; on, it changes nothing yet. Test: `tests/compiler/tests/kani_mode_off_writes_the_same_rust.nika` lowered with and without the switch on a program with a counted loop, a dropped index check and a function with a precondition; the `.stdout` is the comparison's result (`same`).
2. **The crate attributes.** With the switch, the crate's head gets `#[cfg_attr(kani, feature(stmt_expr_attributes, proc_macro_hygiene))]`. Test: the lowered head of the same program with the switch, as `.stdout`.
3. **The harnesses.** With the switch, each function the prover checked (ADR-306 D14: every index and operation proved) gets a `#[cfg(kani)] #[kani::proof_for_contract(name)]` harness whose arguments are `kani::any()`; a `Vec[T]` argument is `kani::vec::any_vec::<T, 8>()` (the bound is the builder's, named in the report; a bigger one is ADR-proof-kani-v1's *not decided*). A function whose argument type has no `kani::Arbitrary` is not harnessed and named in the report of item 4. Test: the lowered harness of the probe program, as `.stdout`.
4. **The report.** With the switch, `nikaia test` writes one line per function not harnessed and why (`not harnessed: f: argument Map[String, i64] has no Arbitrary`). Test: a program with such a function; its report line as `.stdout`.

Done when `nikaia test` with the switch writes a crate that `cargo kani -Z function-contracts -Z loop-contracts` runs (every harness passes, having no contracts yet) on the probe program of the first issue (`a_counted_loop_drops_its_index_check_for_kani.nika`), and without the switch the lowering of `std` and of every test is byte-identical (checked by `lower-std` before and after, its diff empty, quoted). Item 4's commit carries `Fixes #N`. Each surprise is a `Found:` line in the report, never a new issue number.

## Files and limits
* Changes the emitter (`crates/nikaia-std/src/compiler/emit_*.nika`), the tests' driver (`project_tests.nika`) and their lowered `.rs` (output). No Rust by hand.
* Must not change: any byte of the lowering without the switch (`lower-std` of `std` and the tools, diff empty); the build time without the switch (the switch is read once, never per expression).
* Facts: Lowering and lower-std, Tests and the gate, Prover

## Ruled out
* Writing the attributes always, behind `cfg(kani)` only (ADR-proof-kani-v1, option F): costs every build's output size and every reader's eye; D1 refuses it.
* A separate Kani emitter (option G): two emitters drift apart.

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2722).

## Problem

```nika
let pattern = args[1]
process::run("findstr", [pattern, "log.txt"])   // pattern = "/G:secrets.txt"
```

builds today: `process::is_operand` checks only `-`, and Windows programs read a leading `/` as an option.

## To build

1. `process::is_operand` in `crates/nikaia-std/src/runtime/raw_sinks.nika`: false for a leading `-` or `/`, on every target. Its doc comment and help say why.

   - refused: an outside `/x` after `"--"`;
   - passes: `"./" + name`;
   - passes: a `Root::join` path;
   - passes: `is_operand`-guarded.
6. Our own calls are proved, not allowed. Find every caller that now fails (`scripts/solver.nika` hands absolute paths, `drive.nika`, `agent.nika`, `ledgers.nika` and so on) and prove each one through a root or `"./"`. Add no new `untrusted-option` and no `trusted:`.

- The tests pass.

- Part III and the website match.

# Issue #2723: Build ADR-raw-sinks-1 D19: a shell or interpreter named as the program of process::run is a raw sink

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2723).

`blocked`, `safety` · opened 2026-11-22 · updated 2026-11-22 · 7 comments

Builds D19 of [ADR-raw-sinks-1](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/blob/develop/docs/specification/adr/adr-raw-sinks-1.md), the owner's decision on "Decision: a shell named as the program of process::run (sh -c, cmd /c) is a shell sink" (#2717), alternative B.

## Problem

```nika
let name = req.query("file") ?? ""
process::run("sh", ["-c", f"convert {name} thumb.png"])   // name = "x; rm -rf ~"
```

This builds and runs the stranger's text as shell code.

## To build

1. **One list in `std`** (Nikaia, beside `raw_sinks.nika`).
   - Shells: `sh`, `bash`, `zsh`, `dash`, `ksh`, `fish`, `cmd`, `powershell`, `pwsh`.
   - Interpreters: `python`, `python3`, `perl`, `ruby`, `node`, `ssh`.
   - Runners: `env`, `sudo`, `nohup`, `timeout`, `nice`, `xargs`.
   - Match on the base name; ignore `.exe` and case on Windows.
2. **The prover.** When the literal program, or each literal of a D10 `match`, is on the list, every element of `args` with an outside part is refused, `NK1308`, unless `untrusted-shell` is allowed (D4, D5).
   - No predicate clears it.
   - A runner passes the check on to its first operand: the first element not starting with `-`, and after the number for `timeout` and `nice`.
   - That operand is checked as a program under D10.
3. **The run-time check** under `raw-sinks = "warn"` (D7) throws `io::IoError::Other`, naming the program and the argument.
4. **The help** for NK1308 / `untrusted-shell` names the list and says to run the commands with `process::run` one by one instead.
5. **Tests** in `tests/compiler/tests/`, each with its `.stdout`/`.stderr`:
   - refused: `sh -c` with outside text;
   - refused: `/bin/bash`;
   - refused: `env sh -c`;
   - refused: `python3 -c`;
   - refused: `sh -ec`;
   - passes: `sh -c` with a fully literal text;
   - passes: with the key allowed.
6. **Our own calls are proved, not allowed.** `scripts/` and `benches/` have many `process::run("sh", ["-c", …])` calls (`ledgers.nika`, `analysis_cost.nika`, `solver.nika`, `lower_mine.nika`, the benches' `run` helpers, `release.nika`/`pre-push.nika` via `python3`).
   - Every call whose text has an outside part is rewritten without a shell: one `process::run` per command, a pipe as two runs, a glob through `fs`.
   - No `untrusted-shell` allow and no `trusted:` goes into our manifests.
   - A form that cannot yet be written without a shell (e.g. a pipe between two processes) stops the work: `Result: blocked`, with the gap named.
7. **Docs.** Part III 17 (`std::process`) and 13.3 (`untrusted-shell`), and website/safe, state the rule.

## Done when

- The tests pass.
- `scripts/`, `tools/` and `benches/` build under deny with no new allow.
- Part III and the website match.

# Issue #2724: Kani mode: loop invariants from the prover

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2724).

`blocked`, `safety` · opened 2026-11-22 · updated 2026-11-22 · 0 comments

Records ADR-proof-kani-v1 (Kani checks the prover's proofs on the emitted Rust, in a mode of its own); the third of its six issues.
Needs #2721

## Goal
In the Kani mode the emitter writes, on each unchanged `for` loop the prover proved, the invariant the prover used as `#[kani::loop_invariant(…)]`, so Kani checks the induction the prover claims. Loops Kani cannot take a contract on are unwound and reported.

## Governing decision
ADR-proof-kani-v1 D2 (invariants on the unchanged `for`), D4 (the invariant is an obligation, never an assumption), D5 (loops outside Kani's coverage are unwound and reported). ADR-361 D4, D5, D10 (what a loop's invariant is). ADR-306 D19 (a dropped check).

## Today (read in the code)
* The candidate invariant of a loop is built by `bounding_loop_invariant` (`bounds_walk.nika`); the walk's result per function by `bounds_proven` (`bounds_proven.nika`), which takes `through_loops`, `facts` and `ledgers`.
* The emitter writes a `for` in `emit_stmt.nika` (the arm writing `f"{allowed}for {bound} in "`); it does not see the walk's invariants.
* Whether the walk's invariant reaches the emitter at all (it runs in a pass before it) is the first thing item 1 reads; how a fact made in one pass reaches the other is I9's question and the item answers it before any code.

## To build
1. **Hand the invariant over.** The walk records, per loop it proved, the invariant it used, keyed so the emitter finds the loop (the builder names the key and the record; one function all reads go through). With the Kani mode off nothing is recorded. Test: `tests/compiler/tests/kani_mode_writes_the_loop_invariant.nika`, a counted loop over `xs.len()` with a dropped read; its `.stdout` is its output, and the lowered loop with the switch is shown by the issue-1 probe run (quoted in the report).
2. **Write it in Rust.** The invariant's facts are spelled as a Rust boolean over the loop's variables (`0 <= k && (k as usize) <= xs.len()`); a fact with no Rust spelling (a ledger fact over a field, ADR-306 D21) drops the whole invariant for that loop and the loop goes to item 3. Test: the same program with a loop over `xs.iter()` and one with a `while` over a counter.
3. **Unwound and reported.** A loop without an invariant (none proved, no Rust spelling, or a form Kani 0.68 takes no contract on — the forms the first issue recorded) gets nothing on the loop; its harness gets `#[kani::unwind(9)]` (the vector bound of the harness plus one); the report line is `unwound: f: loop at FILE:LINE: <why>`. Test: a loop over a map's `values_mut()`.
4. **A wrong invariant fails.** A test hook writes a deliberately weakened invariant (one fact dropped) for one named loop, so the run shows Kani refusing it. The builder decides where the hook lives (a setting read only in the Kani mode). Test: the run's refusal line as `.stderr`.

Done when, with the Kani mode on, `cargo kani -Z loop-contracts -Z function-contracts` proves every loop of the first issue's probe program by its invariant (no unwinding), refuses the weakened one of item 4, and reports each unwound loop by item 3's line; without the switch the lowering is byte-identical (`lower-std` diff empty, quoted). Item 4's commit carries `Fixes #N`. Each surprise is a `Found:` line in the report, never a new issue number.

## Files and limits
* Changes `bounds_walk.nika` or `bounds_proven.nika` (the record), `emit_stmt.nika` (the attribute) and their lowered `.rs` (output). No Rust by hand.
* Must not change: the walk's verdicts (every `--bounds` row of the suite the same); the lowering without the switch; the walk's time without the switch (nothing is recorded then).
* Facts: Prover, Ledger and bounds proofs, Lowering and lower-std

## Ruled out
* `kani::assume` of the invariant (ADR-proof-kani-v1 D4): it would let a wrong prover pass.
* Rewriting `for` into `while` (option E): Kani takes `for` contracts since 0.66.

# Issue #2725: Kani mode: function contracts and frames from the prover

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2725).

`blocked`, `safety` · opened 2026-11-22 · updated 2026-11-22 · 0 comments

Records ADR-proof-kani-v1 (Kani checks the prover's proofs on the emitted Rust, in a mode of its own); the fourth of its six issues.
Needs #2724

## Goal
In the Kani mode the emitter writes a function's preconditions, its callers' facts it relies on and its frame as Kani function contracts, so Kani checks each function on its own and stubs a checked callee by its contract.

## Governing decision
ADR-proof-kani-v1 D3 (`requires`, `ensures`, `modifies`, `loop_modifies`, `stub_verified`), D4 (only the axioms and a function's own `requires` are assumed; every other fact is an obligation). ADR-269 D5 (a parameter is bounded only by a precondition). ADR-306 D11, D12 (callers' facts).

## Today (read in the code)
* A function's `requires` and `ensures` are written by `emit_contracts.nika` as checks or comments today; the builder reads which.
* The facts a call site hands its callee come from the walk (`bounds_proven`, `bounds_proven.nika`, its `facts`); the frame (what a `mut` parameter may change) from the ledger (`ledgers`).

## To build
1. **`requires` and `ensures`.** With the Kani mode, each Nikaia `requires` / `ensures` the prover used is also written as `#[cfg_attr(kani, kani::requires(…))]` / `kani::ensures(|result| …)`. A clause with no Rust spelling is reported (`no contract: f: requires <text>`) and the function is harnessed without it. Test: `tests/compiler/tests/kani_mode_writes_requires_and_ensures.nika`.
2. **Frames.** A `mut` / `ref mut` parameter's frame becomes `kani::modifies(…)`; a loop changing it gets `kani::loop_modifies(…)`. Test: a function pushing into a `ref mut Vec[i64]` inside a counted loop.
3. **Callees by contract.** A harness of a function calling another checked function gets `#[kani::stub_verified(callee)]`; Kani then checks the call site's facts against the callee's `requires` (an obligation, D4). Test: a caller and a callee with a precondition, the caller's fact proving it.
4. **A wrong fact fails.** The test hook of the third issue, extended to drop one `requires` of a callee: Kani must refuse the caller's harness. Test: the refusal line as `.stderr`.

Done when, with the Kani mode on, `cargo kani -Z function-contracts -Z loop-contracts` proves the contracts of every harnessed function of the four tests above, refuses item 4's weakened one, and reports each clause it could not write; without the switch the lowering is byte-identical (`lower-std` diff empty, quoted). Item 4's commit carries `Fixes #N`. Each surprise is a `Found:` line in the report, never a new issue number.

## Files and limits
* Changes `emit_contracts.nika`, `emit_function.nika` and their lowered `.rs` (output). No Rust by hand.
* Must not change: the lowering without the switch; the checks `requires` emits today.

# Issue #2730: Generated programs and raw-sink test variants find wrong proofs the suite does not reach

[Open and answer this issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Nikaia-Foundation/Nikaia/issues/2730).

`blocked`, `safety` · opened 2026-11-22 · updated 2026-11-22 · 0 comments

Finds wrong proofs and lost refusals the suite's own programs do not reach: generated programs run under debug assertions, and variants of the raw-sink tests that must stay refused.
Found while reviewing pull request #2448 (a change to the raw-sink walk that the tests did not catch until two were pinned: commits "Pin: a join under a root from outside stays a raw sink" and "Pin: a call that is handed the list keeps the checks of a loop over its length").
Part of ADR-proof-kani-v1
Needs #2726

## Goal
A change that makes the prover drop a check it may not drop, or makes the raw-sink walk pass a part it may not pass, is found by a tool before review, not only by a test someone thought to write. Two tools, both run by hand or by the main-only run, never in the develop CI.

## Governing decision
ADR-proof-kani-v1 D7 (the debug-assertions build on `main`) and D8 (what fails is a prover defect, filed with the program). ADR-raw-sinks-1 D2-D6, D11, D13, D14 (what is a raw sink and what passes it; `NK1308`, "data from outside the program at a raw sink"). ADR-306 D19 (the dropped check stays as a `debug_assert!`).

## Today (read in the code)
* A dropped index check is emitted as a `proven::read` (and siblings) whose `debug_assert!` stops with "a proved index is outside: {at} of {len}" (`crates/unsafe/proven-index/src/lib.rs`, `read` and `write`); in a build without debug assertions nothing checks it.
* The tests' driver hands cargo its flags as `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS` and unsets `RUSTFLAGS` (`project_drive.nika`, the function that builds the cargo environment); whether the precompiled std follows is what #2720 measures and #2726 item 1 builds.
* 19 tests expect `NK1308` in their `.stderr` (`grep -l NK1308 tests/compiler/tests/*.stderr`); each is one shape of a raw sink with outside data.
* No generator of Nikaia programs exists in `scripts/`; the fuzzing issues filed (#2556, #2540) fuzz the `unsafe` crates and the regex engines, not the prover.

## To build
1. **A program generator for loops the prover reasons about.** `scripts/prover_fuzz.nika`, run as `nikaia run scripts/prover_fuzz.nika -- --seed S --count N`, writes N small programs from a seed, each a `main` with a list and a loop over it in one of the shapes the prover proves bounds for: an index by the loop variable over `len`, `i + 1` and `i - 1` with and without a guard, a `while` with its own counter, nested loops over two lists, a list grown or shrunk inside the loop, the list handed to a call inside the loop, a slice of it. Sizes and offsets come from the seed. Each program is built and run under `-C debug-assertions=on` through the same driver the suite uses; a program that stops with "a proved index is outside" is written to `target/prover-fuzz/` with its seed and printed. The builder chooses the generator's grammar beyond these shapes. Test: a run with a fixed seed and a small count prints the same program names each time, in the tests' form the builder chooses (`.stdout` beside it).
2. **Variants of the raw-sink tests that must stay refused.** `scripts/raw_sink_variants.nika` reads each test whose `.stderr` expects `NK1308`, writes variants that keep the outside part at the sink: the part bound to a name first, moved into a helper function that hands it back, split from an f-string into `+`, passed through a call the compiler reads, and the guard moved to a value other than the one joined. Each variant is checked with `nikaia check`; a variant without `NK1308` is printed with the test it came from and is a defect of the walk (ADR-proof-kani-v1 D8 by analogy: filed with the program, never answered by changing the test). Test: run over one of the 19 tests, its variants listed in a `.stdout`, each still reported `NK1308`.

Done when `nikaia run scripts/prover_fuzz.nika -- --seed 1 --count 200` and `nikaia run scripts/raw_sink_variants.nika` each run to the end on `develop` and print what they found (or that they found nothing), and each item's test passes; item 2's commit carries `Fixes #N`. Each program or variant found is a `Found:` line in the report with its seed or source test, never a new issue number.
Supervisor: decide whether the main-only workflow of #2726 runs the two tools after the suite.

## Files and limits
* Adds `scripts/prover_fuzz.nika` and `scripts/raw_sink_variants.nika` and their tests; writes only under `target/`.
* Must not change: the prover, the raw-sink walk or any test's expected output (a finding is reported, not fixed here); the develop CI.
* Facts: Tests and the gate, Ledger and bounds proofs

## Ruled out
* An AI review of each pull request as a gate: it advises and can be talked out of a finding by the change it reviews; it may be asked later as advice beside the PR guard, not here.
* Fuzzing the compiler's input bytes at random: almost every input is refused by the parser, so it reaches the prover rarely; the generator writes programs that build.
* Running either tool on every push: their cost is not measured; D7 keeps such runs on `main`.

**Goal.** `html` and `http1` are official packages under `packages/`, not modules of `std`: a program writes `use html` / `use http1`, and the toolchain takes them in by that first `use` as it does `json` and `db` today.
